summary: Missing KMIP certificate after battery replacement prevents FileVault escrow and DEP key upload on refurbished MacBooks
description: Issue summary: After depot battery replacement on several refurbished MacBooks we observed that FileVault escrow (institutional keys) fails to upload to our KMIP-backed escrow service. This prevents DEP/MDM finalization and blocks device check-in for end users. Impact: Devices remain in 'Pending Escrow' state, fail MDM policy application, and cannot complete AAD/AzureAD registration for corporate network access. Environment: Depot-imaged devices (staging) and small sample from production depot-us-west. Reproducible on devices that went through physical battery replacement and SMC/PRAM reset flow.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Receive refurbished MacBook from depot after battery replacement
2) Boot to staging image using our depot netboot and run automated imaging sequence
3) Complete OS install and corporate provisioning agent runs, attempts FileVault escrow upload
4) Provisioning agent reports KMIP upload error and device remains Pending Escrow
5) Attempt manual upload using kms-client returns TLS client cert validation error
logs: ProvisioningAgent[2026-03-09T10:12:03Z] ERROR vault-escrow: kmip upload failed: TLS handshake error: certificate missing for client identity
kms-client --upload --device-serial ABCD1234 exit code 1: client certificate not found in Keychain: 'com.redwood.kmip.client'
system_profiler SMC: hardware: SMC firmware version: 2.58f11; NVRAM: 'boot-args' cleared after SMC reset
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: depot SMC/PRAM reset during battery replacement cleared the local KMIP client certificate entry from the system keychain
Checked keychain on repro device: institutional KMIP cert absent under login/system keychains; provisioning agent expects cert at /Library/Keychains/com.redwood.kmip
Observed that imaging workflow attempts to re-import a device-private cert from /var/lib/provisioning/kmip_backup if present; backup missing for affected devices
Reproduced by intentionally removing KMIP cert before running agent; same error returned
Staging fleet ~5/300 recent repairs affected, correlated to repair vendor batch 'RV-17' which used a different SMC-reset toolchain
temporary_workaround: Manual re-enrollment: run 'sudo security import /opt/repair/kmip-client.p12 -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain -P <pass>' then restart provisioning-agent; confirms KMIP cert present and escrow upload succeeds.
resolution: Engineering to add an idempotent step in the depot imaging sequence to detect missing KMIP client cert and import a freshly generated device-scoped cert from our secure artifact store. Patch PR opened (see related_github_prs). For immediate mitigation we've instructed depot team to preserve /var/lib/provisioning/kmip_backup during battery replacement. Long-term: update vendor repair SOP to avoid SMC tooling that wipes system keychain entries, and add automated cert import to imaging flow.
next_steps: 1) SRE/Imaging to roll the provisioning-agent PR to staging (PR #842) and validate with 20 repaired units - target 2026-03-16
2) Depot ops to audit last 300 repairs from vendor RV-17 and run manual re-enroll script for affected serials - target 2026-03-15
3) Security to rotate escrow MFA key if we detect any missing cert anomalies during audit - target 2026-03-20
4) Create vendor-facing repair SOP update to prevent keychain wipes - assigned to Sofia Martinez - due 2026-03-22
